newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French household spending July/August.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French household spending July/August.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on French household spending figures released by statistics institute INSEE, which showed a 3.0 percent rise in August, driven by car sales, after a 0.6 percent drop in July.
"The data suggests a strong rebound in spending in the third quarter as people were expecting.

But, as INSEE suggests, the big bounce was due to car sales with incentives (scheme), so there could be renewed weakness in the fourth quarter. Car sales are continuing strong in September so the suggestion is the third quarter spend will be strong."
"As expected car sales were up about 20 percent, but having said that overall consumer spending seems very strong. The problem is the pattern is very erratic.
Ex-autos it's still up 0.5, so it's not just the big one-off factor. We may still see further progress in September. It all adds up to strong third quarter growth.

There's still the problem of how spending will behave as the (government car buying) incentive disappears. There may be a decline (in spending) in the fourth quarter but maybe by then other factors will come in, like investment and stock building."

"We already knew car sales had been very strong in August so the surprise is not in car sales. There's a possible surprise in the sense that durables, white and brown products that is, have performed very well.

The third quarter is likely to be very bullish. I previously forecast a quarter-on-quarter (spending rise of) 0.7 percent and I'm revising that to 1.2 pct. I'm now confident of 1.1 percent GDP growth in third quarter.

That said, car sales in September will be even higher than in August, but the price will be a fourth quarter which will turn out negative in terms of consumption. Over the full year 1996 consumption will be much higher than anyone had expected including the government. 1997 will start with a negative."
